summary: Regex detectors scanned on sample notes isolate six properties that are exactly 0/1 by label in every sample and independent coin flips in the corpus (greeting, closing block, hashtag, quote, parenthetical, female pronouns). Dependence is measured with the gradient-times-activation proxy, first by corpus regressions (in-pair, pooled with topic dummies, in-pair vs out-pair), then by single-property removal edits and pronoun flips on sample notes, normalized by a corpus topic coefficient. One disagreement (probe 3 quote) is settled with true logits on with/without-quote pairs. Latents come from pooled per-latent edit deltas times gradient, chosen greedily under a topic-contribution cap, with a cue-balancing alternation for the two-cue probe. Regexes are scored against the detectors on corpus and samples.

per_probe.conclusion: closing block (sign-off line and/or name line)
per_probe.procedure: Closing was one of six properties perfectly tied to label. Corpus in-pair and pooled regressions gave closing dependence about 0.41-0.46, everything else small; single-property removal on 8 notes per class gave 0.457 with low SE, next largest quote about 0.1. Latents: per-latent closing contribution from removal deltas pooled over all probes times probe 0 gradient, greedy up to 16 with a cap on removed topic contribution. Regex: sign-off phrase alternation on its own line, scope any, scored against the closing detector on corpus and samples. Ablation check on sample notes kept class separation.

per_probe.conclusion: greeting first line, plus closing block
per_probe.procedure: Greeting dependence about -1.37 in pooled regression and edits. Closing was borderline (0.20-0.27 across six estimates); round 2 removed closing from 24 class-1 notes (0.261) and added synthetic closings to 16 class-0 notes (0.122). Kept as a second cue because it stood clearly above the 0.09-0.12 maxima of probes 2 and 3. Latents: pooled greeting and closing deltas times gradient; alternating picks for whichever cue was less removed, 16 total under a topic cap, split 8/8 across the two cue entries. Regexes: greeting detector on first line, closing sign-off regex on any scope.
per_probe.quote: Probe 1's `closing` (0.20–0.27 across six methods, real closings) is qualitatively distinct from the max in probes 2/3 (~0.09–0.12), so it's a genuine second cue.

per_probe.procedure: Corpus regressions left greeting and closing in the ambiguous band. Round 2 edits on 16 notes per class removed every present property and flipped pronouns; all dependences came out at or below about 0.12 (quote highest), with closing and greeting near zero. Answered none.

Corpus estimates put quote at 0.15-0.32 while removal edits gave about 0.04 with high variance. After confirming the quote editor worked, true logits were taken for three class-1 notes with and without the quote: deltas differed in sign (proxy deltas did too), so quote was judged not a cue. All other properties small. Answered none.
per_probe.quote: the **true** quote deltas for probe 3 are also inconsistent in sign (+1.55, −0.22, −0.70; mean ≈ +0.21), confirming quote is **not a cue**

caveats: Several outputs are truncated in the log (probe 2/3 rows of the regressions, edit effects and corpus per-topic table; probe 1 greedy output), so some values used in decisions are known only from later notes. How the 16 probe-1 latents were split 8/8 between the greeting and closing entries is not shown; the script assigns each latent to the cue it was picked for, which is a guess. The round-1 pronoun effect initially oriented the sign by label and was corrected in round 2 to use the detector; the script uses the corrected rule throughout. The round-1 normalizer was the pooled-regression topic coefficient typed in as constants. Final decisions for probe 1 closing and probe 2 combine several estimates by judgment.
